body:
`scripts/extract_spa_strings.py --write` regenerates the AUTOGEN block from
statically-parseable frontend literals. Anchors added by hand INSIDE that block
for strings the parser cannot see (dynamic keys, runtime-built values) are
removed without warning — measured 2026-08-09: 72 removed / 37 added, net 31
lost, including "contains" and "begins with".

The loss is silent twice over. `--write` reports only a count ("530 anchored
msgid(s)"), never a delta, and the damage does not surface until the NEXT
`Update Translations` run marks the now-unextracted msgids obsolete, dropping
real translations from the compiled `.mo`. That run is tagged `[skip ci]`, so
no test reports it either. fr/ru/de lost human-authored translations this way
and main went red on a commit nobody tested.

Fix direction: `--write` should refuse to remove an anchor whose msgid still
carries a translation in any locale, and should print the add/remove delta
rather than a total. The hand-maintained section above the marker (added in
#1485) prevents recurrence but does not make the generator safe.
title: extract_spa_strings.py --write silently discards hand-added anchors
